about: Reconstructed scripted story scenes (no fight). The original server drove their stages with an encounter script the client does not ship. Each scene is a sequence of steps; a step names the DungeonQuestConfig quest the tracker shows (var 10001) and its goal counter (var 10003), the scene actors the server shows during it (client NPCConfig ids at scene-editor points, with the buffs that open their interactions), an optional story the client plays (dungeon var 100020016), the client events that complete it, and an optional teleport after it. A quest of the scene that only a branch the reconstruction cannot reach would show is listed under "unplayed" with its reason. Every decision carries its reason and the scene its confidence; what is guessed is listed per scene. Switch: Ro3Emu:ReconstructedDungeons. Never mixed into client data.

contract.interaction: 32700 NpcInteractionReq {npc_uid, interaction_id} on a scene actor: the client sends it from LC_DAL_Interact.SendNPCInteractionReq when the player presses the interaction's skill button (InteractMode 3 ClickSkillIcon), walks into range (2 AutoInteractWhenInRange) or a dialogue option runs action 211 TriggerNpcInteract (LC_InteractActions.lua:5672-5698). The interaction must be one of the actor's NPCConfig _iInteractID; the server answers 32700 with the request echoed (LC_InteractManager._onInteractResponse then runs the client-hosted actions, e.g. 53 NPCInteractDialogue).
contract.message: The NPCInteractConfig _iEXECAction ["210", id, ...] of that interaction: ActionConfig 210 SendDungeonMessage is server-hosted (_iEXECHost 1), so the client never runs it; it is the dungeon script's own message id (LC_InteractManager.lua:1975-2030 runs only client/all-hosted actions).
contract.gate: An interaction's _iNPCCondition 1004 CheckHaveBuff (LC_CommonCondition.lua:180-196) asks whether the actor carries a BuffConfig group (_iBuffID). The client shows the button only then, so the step that waits on an interaction gives its actor that buff.
contract.story: Dungeon var 100020016 (DungeonVariableFunctionConfig: start function PlayCutSceneStory, array) with [plot] makes the client play PlotInterpretation <plot> (LC_DunGeon_Actions.lua:3476-3490, LC_CutSceneManager.PlayStory). At its end (also when skipped) the plot's action 601 VideoPerformEndClient sends 84011 PlotActingEnd {plotId} (LC_GuildServer.PlotActionEnd), its action 150 PlotActingTrigger sends 84012 {plotId} (LC_TaskHelper.PlotActingTriggerReq), and 32709 follows; either one completes the step, neither expects a reply. Sent once in a 30404 DungeonEventDungeonVarChange: LC_DunGeon_Base._pushDungeonVars calls the function on every push, so it is never kept in the 30401 snapshot.
contract.region: The scene editor's server regions (regionType 2; no client consumer registers them with LC_TriggerAreaManager, so the client never reports them): the server tests the participant's walked position with LC_AreaHelper.CheckInArea's geometry (shapeType 1 circle radius = length, 2 rectangle length x width turned by direction).
contract.point: No region exists; the participant's walked position within radius metres of the scene-editor point (inferred).

guessed: Timing, places and order from the official video (Ragnarok 3 Genesis, 33:05 on; the scene loads at about 33:19): 13 s of calm with 5300540/5300541; at 33:33 a shell bursts at mark 59 and its fire stays; the startled crew's bubbles and the lines follow, the Chief comes down from the prow, and at 33:40 two pirate ships come up to port, the Evil Boss showing off on the nearer one; stage 2 begins at 34:00 while the tracker still read 'Have a Chitchat with them'. So stage 1 runs on the scene's clock (13 s calm, 25 s attack).

The startled crew (5300061-5300065, whose bubble interactions 5300048-5300052 have no condition) replace the calm crew when the shell hits; their bubbles play on the scene's clock as 32700 replies (the client plays a bubble from any reply), and also when the player walks up to them.

Ships lie parallel to the deck (its long side runs along z, the prow at +z): each comes up sailing along z and stops 30-50 m off; the cannons' three to starboard (east), two at once and the third later from astern, the pirates' two to port. The editor's patrols 95-97 and 64 come in broadside and are not used. Where a deck lies on a ship model is not in the client data: 7 m above its root (4.2 m on the small one).

The shot: template 61202 (the GVE turret's) instead of 53530: the same fire, ball and blast prefabs with their sounds; the ball flies at 200 m/s, one at the ship aimed at. Three hits sink a ship, each showing about 9.9 million (the video's numbers; the ship still takes three).
While the ships live, their fire lands on the deck every 12 s, by turns at 60 and 59 (a 2.5 s marker ring, then the blast and 8 s of fire). It hurts nobody: a gunner cannot step away from it.

Stage 3 is one fight of nine (0/9): the ships collide 6 s in, the pirates leave their deck, the five warriors drop in with their FallDown at the Boss's 'Charge!' and the four archers 13 s later. The warriors' and archers' special skills are their boss skill books (BossSkillSets).

Wule, Boya and the Eden Group Chief fight beside the player through the boarding and the Boss (5300086-5300088, camp 1, whose AI 5300007 is not in the client): they go for the nearest monster and swing their skills; a hit takes 1 % of its maximum HP (3 % for a special). The monsters never turn on them.

At 29 % of the Evil Boss's HP (35:44) a blast shakes the ship, its fire burns whoever stands within 4.5 m every second, and two rows of barrels appear: five rolling along patrols 69-72 and 98, five across the deck at z 470; a barrel bursts when the fight comes within 1.5 m of it.

Stage 5 ends when the player walks up to the prow or after 15 s; the crew walk back to their posts (patrols 103-105). After the captain's dialogue the tracker goes back to stage 5 while four shells burst around him, then the closing cutscene (PlotInterpretation 130161, its QTE, then 130162 or 130163) ends the scene.

guessed: The game is inferred as a whole from its lines: Moonlight Flower opens with her three bubbles (5310011-5310013); each round warns 'I'm about to catch you! Watch out!' (5310005), shows the 5 s countdown tip 'Hide in the darkness and don't let them Discover you!' (5310010) three seconds later and looks when it runs out. A player standing within 3 m of a group 27 point passes the round; anyone else is found ('Play with me again~', 5310014) and the game starts over.

Two rounds, from 'Play with me a little longer!' (5310006) after the first and 'I had a great time~' (5310007) after the last. A passed round searches every darkness point within 8 m of where the player hid, so the next round needs another side of the room.

The darkness is read as group 27: its 42 server spawn points ring the open centre where the player is born, away from Moonlight Flower. What the original spawned there (seekers, moonlight or hiding places) is not named by the client data, and the player gets no hidden status there.

Moonlight Flower (400097) stands at point 26, turned away from the room (direction 0) like a seeker counting; point 25, the same place facing the born point, is presumably where she talked to the player.
The 1.5 s between the opening bubbles, the 3 s warning and the 3 s pause after a look are chosen, not data.
